subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.
reasoning:
I'm planning a brutalist housing block model, static with no joints needed, drawing inspiration from Unité d'Habitation, Barbican, and Trellick Tower — thinking a slab block raised on pilotis as the core design direction.

I'm sketching concrete dimensions: around 60m length, 20m depth, 12 floors at 3m each plus a 6m pilotis base, facing +Z and centered at x=0. The structure will use tapered concrete columns, exposed floor slabs, vertical party-wall fins framing loggias, and a stepped-relief facade in the Corbusier polychrome style, topped with a rooftop terrace and ventilation stacks, plus a separate connected service tower.

Rather than creating hundreds of individual bay parts, I realize I can use a custom paint function on a single core wall box: computing bay and floor indices from surface position to procedurally draw windows, frames, and colored panels based on a hash. This collapses the whole facade detail into one part, so now I'm working out the texel density needed for the paint sheet given the total painted area.

Actually, a generated SVG texture might give even sharper resolution than paint sheets for the window grid, so I'm comparing that approach's pixel density against the paint option before deciding which to use.

I'll have separate textures per facade — front with full glazing, back with kitchen-sized windows, and the gable end — since that's where the building's real character comes through. Behind these textured planes sits the plain board-marked concrete core, while the loggia back walls get the detail treatment: window, door, colored side panel, and a parapet strip marking each floor slab edge.

Now I'm counting parts: slab edges with parapets across all floors, plus paired fins on each loggia bay, to make sure the geometry stays manageable.

Thinking about Unité-style color accents on loggia back walls rather than the fin sides, keeping fins pure concrete while texture handles the colored panels. I'm also considering thickening the fins slightly and adding a stepped penthouse/roof terrace level to break up the massing with brutalist variation.

I'm sketching in more rooftop elements -- a ventilation stack, a curved access ramp, and a mid-building shops level around floors 7-8 drawn with continuous ribbon glazing and vertical mullions instead of colored loggias. I'm also thinking about adding a separate tall service tower at one end, Trellick-style, as another massing move.

For the tower texture, I'm planning to wrap the same SVG drawing across all box faces with a viewBox matching the tower's proportions, using alpha cutouts so only the drawn concrete color shows while keeping it consistent with the painted concrete elsewhere.

I'll also write a custom procedural paint shader for the concrete — warm-grey tones with board-marking lines, mottling, and dark streaks below ledges for weathering — using noise and mix utilities, and mirror similar streaking in the SVG facade textures. For the facade SVG itself, I'm sizing the viewBox to match real-world proportions (roughly 10 units per meter) so the texture resolution stays consistent across the building face.

Now I'm working out floor and slab positioning: each floor spans 3m starting at y=6, with 0.4m-thick slabs at each level and a roof slab capping the stack at y=42, with parapet and superstructure elements layered above that.

For the facade texture mapping, I'm figuring out orientation so the front plane facing +Z reads correctly from the viewer's perspective — confirming that aiming with the z-axis puts local +X toward world +X, so the image displays unmirrored when viewed from the front, and I'll need to handle the back facade's orientation separately.

Now I'm laying out the SVG floor-by-floor, mapping each floor index to its vertical band in the 360-unit image, then structuring each bay's loggia with a shadowed background rect and a colored panel for the wall between the fins.

Within each panel I'm placing the window/door glazing — a glass rectangle with mullions dividing it into thirds, a balcony door on one side, a sill below, and the surrounding panel color filling the rest of the bay.

I'm also adding a shadow gradient overlay at the top of each loggia for depth, reusing a single defined gradient across all bays, and picking an accent color palette (red, yellow, blue, cream, green, orange) similar to Unité d'Habitation's colored side panels against mostly neutral walls.

Deciding to keep panel colors applied to full bays rather than splitting them, and planning the shop floor level with dark ribbon glazing and regular mullions. I'll sparingly add a couple of glowing accents instead — a red warning beacon on the rooftop and lit entrance lights — rather than making window glow pervasive across the whole facade.

For the back facade, I'm designing smaller windows per bay with occasional stair lighting and a muted two-accent palette, keeping similar fin detailing but less colorful overall. For the end gables, I'm thinking blank concrete walls with diagonal stair slit windows, possibly a large painted emblem or number, with stair towers connected by bridges at one end.

On the opposite gable, I like the idea of a giant stylized Modulor figure as a relief mural — a man with a raised arm alongside spiral scale motifs in red and blue, rendered as a concrete relief with shadow and highlight to give it depth as a bold architectural emblem.

Now for the pilotis supports, I'm planning two rows of 11 sculptural columns spaced across the base, each tapering dramatically like legs — narrow near the ground, pinching in at mid-height, then flaring wider at the top — built using a loft with multiple width/height stations to get that iconic Unité silhouette.

For the pilotis I'll make them thin fin-like columns, narrow along x but wide along z like structural walls under the building. Then I'm adding a recessed glass lobby volume at ground level between the column rows, centered at the building's midpoint with a lift core rising through the pilotis.

Now I'm sketching the lobby's glass facade with doors and mullions, plus a projecting entry canopy slab out front. For the roof, I'm planning a low parapet wall around the edge and considering a curved vault form for the gym or crèche block on top.

I'm adding rooftop elements inspired by Unité d'Habitation: tapered ventilation chimneys made via lathe geometry, a stair/lift head box, a sloped pavilion, a shallow paddling pool, a sculptural ramp up to the pavilion, a curved solarium wall, and a pergola of repeating concrete T-beams with cylindrical water tanks.

Now I'm planning a separate Trellick-style stair tower positioned off the main block, linked by glazed bridges every three floors, with a crowning element at the top of the tower.

Writing texture and scale logic...

I'll match the texture tones to the painted concrete mid-tone, add a gable stair bulkhead on the rooftop crown, and keep ground treatment minimal with just entry steps and a canopy rather than a full plinth. I'm budgeting around 15 flat colors out of 64 and confirming the model's overall scale—80m wide, 52m tower height, with everything sitting flush at y=0.

For board-marked concrete detailing, I'm working out the texel density needed given the massive painted surface area across slabs, columns, and tops—estimating roughly 30k m² total, which points to about a 10cm texel resolution to support 0.2m board-mark lines.

To cut down on cost, I'm considering using flat concrete colors with slight random tonal variation (from a handful of grey shades) for most slabs and fins, reserving actual painted board-mark textures for visible hero elements like the core box, roof structures, columns, and tower. I'm now sizing the core box's face area, noting its front/back will mostly be hidden by text anyway.

Actually box mapping could share one texture across all 42 fins since horizontal stretching won't matter for vertical streak patterns — the board-mark lines stay at consistent vertical spacing regardless of face width. I'm sizing the texture resolution based on meters-per-pixel for a 36m tall fin.

For slabs, I'll skip detailed texturing and just use flat concrete color variations for the fascia and parapet railing instead, reserving the paint budget for columns and the core box which total around 10k area.

I'm settling on a 2048 paint sheet size giving roughly 6cm texel density, applied to columns, core sides/top, roof details, lobby, and tower crown, while slabs/fins/parapets stay texture-based or flat. For the atlas, I'm planning around seven texture maps (facade front/back, fins, tower, mural, lobby, bridge) plus the paint sheet, shrinking facade textures to 1600 so everything fits within a 4096 atlas.

Now I'm defining helper functions for creating static box parts with color and texture tinting, placing them at their bounding centers without any joints since these are static props and scenery rather than articulated geometry.

I'm picking a flat concrete color palette with several shade variants, then writing a procedural paint function that mixes noise-based tones for the base concrete and adds board-mark streaking on vertical faces... 

Writing paint shader code...

Still refining noise sampling...

I should also darken underside faces and add subtle green lichen tint on upward-facing surfaces. Now moving to actual dimension constants for the tower structure—length, core depth, loggia depth, floor count and height, base height—before writing the texture generation helpers.

Working out bay widths, core box dimensions, and slab placements: slabs span the full width with slight overhang beyond the gables, extend in depth, and include parapet lips at front and back for the brutalist look.

Now I'm adding vertical fins at each bay boundary running the full building height, positioned along the front and back loggia faces, matching up with the gable edges at the extremes.

Then I'm figuring out the roof: the top slab sits above the core and extends beyond it, with a parapet ring of four boxes running around all sides built from flat-colored concrete panels, and I'm starting to lay out the various roof elements like the gym enclosure within the parapet boundary.

Moving to the overall facade, I'm laying out pavilions left to right, starting with a nursery block on the far left featuring a barrel-vault roof made from a half-cylinder shape springing from low walls, with a painted yellow-ochre front wall for a Corbusier-style accent.

Building the vault geometry...

Still working out the stack geometry... Then I'll add the elevator overrun as a chamfered box near the roof, and sketch a pergola/solarium frame on the right side with concrete posts, transverse beams, and a slatted board roof.

I'm also planning a colorful paddling pool as a low rim box with a blue water plane, and a straight inclined concrete ramp connecting the roof to the stair/lift block, built as a wedge-shaped extruded solid with railings.

For the tower, I'm defining the square shaft rising to 47 units, topped by a cantilevered crown plant room with an overhanging box and roof cap slab, finished with louvre texturing.

Now I'm adding beacon details—small red glow spheres at the cap's corners plus a thin mast with a glowing red tip—then working out connecting bridges at floors 1, 4, 7, and 10, giving each bridge box ribbon windows along its long faces and concrete texturing to tie into the tower.

Adding four corner piers with concrete paint tone, checking their proportions look right. Now I'm sanity-checking the lobby footprint against the pilotis column grid to make sure they don't collide.

I need to shrink the column z-extent and pull the lobby in a bit to avoid overlap, then give the lobby front face a decal with doors, glass mullions, and maybe a signage text for the building name.

Positioning the entry canopy to clear the columns, then adding a few cantilevered steps near the center. For the pilotis zone I'm sketching tapered pier shapes like Unité's, building frustum boxes that narrow from base to top as structural supports.

Writing frustum column geometry...

I'm also planning a mural plane on the west gable face, positioned just outside the core box with its orientation facing outward.

Good, that confirms +Z reads as the viewer's right. Now I'm thinking through the gable treatment on the +X tower side, and working out how the core box faces stay hidden behind offset facade planes at z=±6.01. I also need to account for loggia depth—fins and slabs extending to z=8.2 with the parapet at 8.1—while making sure the SVG facade doesn't double up with the visible 3D slab.

Writing SVG code...

I'm working through realistic proportions here, comparing to Corbusier-style loggias with floor-to-ceiling heights, slabs, and parapets to figure out how tall the visible window band should be. Settling on a 0.7m parapet, I'm planning the wall panel so the left third reads as a glazed balcony door and the right two-thirds as a window with a sill, keeping the hidden lower portion behind the parapet irrelevant to the drawing.

Now I'm sketching the SVG details: the door and window glass rects with frame lines, a shadow gradient under each floor, cream/color accent panels for a checkered facade look, and weathering streaks like grime gradients at window sills and under fins. I'm also planning a separate back facade function with muted colors, strip windows, and stair-landing slits, plus a dark glass band for the ground-floor shops.

For the fin texture, I'm defining a tall narrow viewBox with plank-line rects spaced for subtle board texture, random opacity variations per plank for tonal variety, and drip-stain marks beneath each floor level, estimating the whole thing lands around 700 lines of code using a seeded random function for consistent scatter effects.

For the mural texture, I'm sketching a tall gable viewBox with a concrete base and subtle board lines, then outlining a Modulor-style human figure using basic shapes for the head, torso, raised arm, and legs with a relief-style lighter fill.

Adding streaks like fin marks, and checking the gable plane dimensions at x=-30.02 to confirm it spans the correct width and height for the roof slab.

The slab ends protrude slightly beyond the core, so I need the mural plane shaded between the slabs — that should work fine. Now I'm setting up the tower texture viewBox dimensions for the 6m × 47m scale.

Drawing the base concrete and staggered vertical stair slit windows...

I'll drop the doors and instead cover the bridge connection points at the face. For the tower, I'm aligning floor rows to 30-unit increments in SVG coordinates, with ground at the base and rows numbered upward from there, matching bridge levels to tower floors. For lighting, I'm adding red beacons at the mast and tower, plus a separate glowing amber plane for a lit doorway effect near the lobby.

I'm building the lobby with a concrete box and glowing amber glass door panels, then adding scattered glowing amber strips in some shop-floor bays to simulate lit interiors behind the darker glass facade.

For upper floor windows, I want a scattered pattern of randomly lit amber window planes, and I'm considering merging all those plane geometries into a single part using mergeGeometries to keep the part count efficient instead of creating dozens of separate parts.

Converting the SVG mapping to a glow plane position with lit windows layered over dark glass, keeping colors mostly restrained concrete tones with a few Corbusier accent colors in specific spots. Now I'm starting to write the actual module imports and setup for the scene builder.

Writing concrete paint function...

Adding streak noise for wood grain darkening and dirt staining toward the base...

Writing SVG markup...

Drawing doors and glass windows with gradient fills, mullion frames, and shading overlays for depth...

I'm adding a weathering overlay with random dark streaks across the facade, then randomly populating window lights for the front and back faces, skipping the shop floor. Next I'm setting up geometry helper functions for building boxes and textured boxes to construct the brutalist housing block.

Building the slab loop...

I'll skip the brise-soleil detail and keep the parapet on the shop floor for simplicity. For the roof, I'm defining a parapet ring using boxes along the perimeter edges at the slab top height.

Now I'm positioning roof structures: a nursery pavilion centered at x=-22 with walls and a vaulted half-cylinder roof, working out the scale needed so the vault radius matches the wall width in z.

I'll add a yellow accent panel and dark window/door details to the nursery's front face, then move on to laying out the x-axis positions for the remaining structures, starting with the nursery spanning roughly -28 to -16.

Next I'm placing the pool with its rim around x=-9, plus three cylindrical stacks behind it at staggered x positions. I'm also sketching the lift head and chimney on the opposite side, and working out a ramp that rises from ground level toward a platform near the gym area.

Still writing ramp geometry...

Now I'm adding the lift head structure with a recessed slot window, then laying out the pergola with corner and mid posts, plus long beams and cross slats on top.

I'm placing two water tank cylinders with conical lids near the tower, then working on the mast with its rod, beacon sphere, and aviation warning lights on the crown corners, and finally sketching the lobby box dimensions.

For the lobby front I'm designing a glazed entrance with a concrete portal frame, dark glass mullion panels, and central doors, adding amber glow planes over the door areas to suggest an illuminated interior, with a matching but ungloved glass plane on the back.

Now I'm sketching the canopy structure with its supporting columns and fascia, plus entry steps, and planning to add "HOUSING BLOCK 9" signage text on the lobby's top fascia band.

For textures, I'm designing the tower louvre and crown pattern, concrete corner piers, and a bridge texture showing concrete bands with glass strips and mullions, then positioning that bridge geometry between two towers.

Now I'm computing the tower's shaft and crown geometry, setting the shaft height to 46.6 with a crown section above it up to 51.2, adding a cap slab and mast on top, and verifying the bridging aligns with the tower's footprint before placing corner piers.

I'm deciding to skip extra details like a tower base plinth, expansion joints, and a secondary rear entrance to keep things simple, and finalizing the texture list at eight entries covering finish, facades, mural, tower, crown, bridge, and lobby materials.

For the lit window glow, I'm building planes oriented correctly for both front and back facades using rotation and translation so each faces outward properly, mapping the back facade's texture coordinates to mirror the front's so the image reads correctly from behind, and positioning the glowing window panes so they stay visible above the parapet line.

Checking the textured white part looks fine, then thinking through concrete color hierarchies for the structure versus the darker roof parapets. I'm considering extra distinctive details like a brise-soleil of vertical concrete mullions across the shop floor bays, but deciding to skip the pilotis plinth and underside soffit coloring for now to keep things simpler.

I'm placing the mullions within the loggia near the shop floor level, skipping the parapet for that particular floor since it's a commercial space, and sizing the fins reasonably. I'm also weighing whether to add colored accent panels to the fin sides in the Corbusier style but deciding that could add too much complexity.

Instead I'm merging those colored panels into a smaller set of grouped boxes rather than one per bay, applying a color to roughly 30% of bays per floor, keeping geometry efficient by batching boxes with indexed geometry, and positioning the colored accent panel on one side of each selected bay's fin.

I'm planning to share a single bay-color generation function between the SVG texture creation and panel placement logic, so both stay consistent. I also need to work out texture atlas sizing — packing front/back facade SVGs plus other panels into a 4096² sheet while keeping texel counts reasonable.

Writing SVG facade generation code...

Writing window and door details...

Still writing facade details...

Adding seam lines and drip stain streaks...

Still drawing the Modulor figure...

Still designing the building SVGs...

Adding glow planes for side panes...

Now I'm placing pilotis columns along x, but need to skip the one at x=0 since it would land right in front of the lobby door. Keeping other columns spaced beside the canopy and entry steps.

Working through the frustum box dimensions for the pilotis, tapering from the ground to the slab underside around y=5.8-5.9, then setting up the roof lathe profile with concrete coloring.

For the water tank, I'm deciding between a lathe shape and a simpler combination of cylinder and cone geometries.

Now I'm building the ramp with an extrusion function and then working out the pool geometry—a concrete rim box with a water surface box set at a slightly lower height to create a sunken, recessed water effect.

I realize the rim needs to be built as four separate wall segments rather than a solid box, so the water box can actually sit visibly inside the opening. I'm skipping loungers and cranes for now, and starting to tally up the total part count across columns, slabs, fins, and facade elements.

Adding up roof, tower, and lobby pieces, I land around 270 total parts. I'm working out mullion placement at the shop floor level inside the loggia, checking the core box dimensions and material against the slab, confirming the roof parapet hides the core top, verifying the tower bridges cleanly to the main slab without gaps, and noting the glow kit's import path.

Now I'm setting up a seeded random function to scatter lit windows across the facade, collecting warm and pale window geometries into arrays and computing their size and position from the SVG window coordinates to place plane geometries at the right spots on each floor.

Adding shop floor lit planes for the front facade, reusing the same shop-floor geometry on the back without front-only lighting, and merging the plane geometries into a single group colored with the warm glow tones before passing it to the glow helper with the matching material color.

Now I'm defining the building constants — floor count, floor height, base height, panel width, and shop-floor offset — and computing total height and width from them. I'm iterating through the facade panel grid, creating thin box geometries for each non-shop, non-cream panel, grouping them by color so they can be merged and rendered efficiently.

Adding fin placement logic...

I'm positioning the mural plane and starting to write a helper function that generates a concrete-textured SVG background with optional board-line patterns.

Adding streak and drip details...

Still writing tower SVG...

Adding random opacity patches for concrete tone variety, then I'll set up the build function structure with module-level color constants for slabs, dark accents, steel, and glass before writing the main builder logic.

Rounding out the palette with warm oranges, pale tones, and blues, then planning the roof details, ramp walls, glowing rooftop beacons, and a stair/lift tower before finalizing the extrude parameters.

Writing decal and glow plane helpers...

Now I'm working out the vault geometry using a half-cylinder shape, rotating it so the flat face aligns correctly and checking the math on which half gets kept after the rotation, then scaling it down vertically to flatten the arch.

Checking that the vault position and width line up with the wall tops and z-extent so everything meets seamlessly. Moving on to the nursery front wall with an ochre panel and window cutout, positioning them against the front face, and leaving the skylight slots and door cutout as optional additions for now.

Now placing the stack elements with plinth bases at specific x positions, then building the lift head structure with its concrete box, a glass slot on the front face positioned to align with the wall, and an overhanging roof cap slab above it.

Next I'm working out the ramp and platform geometry, extending the platform to cover the ramp's endpoint, adding a parapet railing along its front edge, then laying out a pergola structure with posts positioned to align with the platform and lift head footprint.

Adding beams and slats...

Now I'm placing water tanks beyond the lift head's footprint, checking cylinder radii against the parapet boundary so they fit within the overall envelope.

I'm sanity-checking the rng helper signature against the kit's docs to confirm it returns a proper random function, then finalizing the text box tint color before writing out the complete answer.
